name: epoc
description: Read your meetings recorded with epoc, the Android meeting recorder: list them and read their transcripts. Read-only.

interface.longDescription:
epoc records meetings on your Android phone and transcribes them as people talk, in 60 languages, even mixed in one meeting, with each speaker kept apart. Recordings are kept on your phone; audio is never synced to epoc's cloud.

With Your agents turned on in the app, epoc syncs the text of the meetings you choose to share, encrypted, and this plugin lets ChatGPT read them, even when your phone is off. Ask the way you'd ask a colleague who was there: what was decided, who owns which action item, what a customer objected to, what changed since last week. ChatGPT finds the meeting and reads its transcript.

Two tools, both read-only:
- list_meetings lists your synced meetings, newest first, with each one's title, start time, duration, languages, speakers and number of transcript pages. It can narrow the list to a range of dates.
- get_transcript returns one page of a meeting's transcript: who spoke, what they said, and when in the meeting. Long meetings come in several pages.
The plugin can't change, delete or send anything.

To connect:
1. In the epoc app, open Settings, then Your agents, and tap Turn on. Sign in, write down your recovery key, and choose which meetings to share.
2. In ChatGPT, add epoc and sign in with the same account. epoc's page names ChatGPT; choose Allow.
3. Approve the request in epoc on your phone within 5 minutes. The page continues on its own, and ChatGPT is connected.

Privacy: your meetings are encrypted on your phone with a key that only your phones and the assistants you approve hold, and audio is never synced. epoc's cloud decrypts a meeting only in memory while an assistant you approved reads it, and its logs hold counts, never titles, names or words. What ChatGPT reads goes to OpenAI, as with anything you share with it. You choose which meetings are shared, and you can stop sharing one or unlink ChatGPT in the app at any time.

You need epoc on an Android phone and an epoc account, which you create when you turn on Your agents. epoc is for people 18 and over.
defaultPrompt: What action items came out of my latest weekly sync, and who owns each one?
Summarise my last customer interview: what did they need, and what held them back?
Which meetings did I have in the last two weeks? One line on each.

positive.description: The user asks for the action items of their most recent weekly sync. ChatGPT finds the meeting and reads its one transcript page.
positive.prompt: What action items came out of my most recent weekly product sync, and who owns each one?
positive.expected_behavior: Three action items, each with its owner and deadline: Priya ships the PDF export fix for right-to-left (Hebrew) text in the build going out on Thursday; Tom designs a screen that explains the battery exemption before the system asks, added to the new onboarding, ready for review on Tuesday; Daniel sends Harbor Lane Dental the annual invoice quote for twelve seats by Monday, copying Maya, at the annual price with two months free. It may add that the Settings link to Noa's help article on deleting an account goes on the next release's list.

positive.description: The user asks what a pricing meeting decided. ChatGPT reads it and separates the decisions from the open question.
positive.prompt: What did we decide in the pricing review, and what's still open?
positive.expected_behavior: Decided: Option A, two tiers, Personal at 6 euros a month for 10 hours and Pro at 14 euros a month for 40 hours (rather than Option B, one plan at 9 euros for 20 hours plus 50 cents an extra hour); paying for a year gets two months free (60 euros for Personal, 140 for Pro); the free tier stays at three hours a month; the subscribers on the 9-euro launch price (about 120) move to Pro and keep 9 euros. Open: whether to round prices to a flat 6 and 14 euros in every country, tax included; Priya asks the accountant what that costs and brings the number to next week's sync.

positive.description: The user asks for a summary of a customer interview, split into needs and objections.
positive.prompt: Summarise my customer interview with Juniper Street Bakery: what does Grace need, and what are her objections?
positive.expected_behavior: Needs: a dated written record of her phone calls. Suppliers: the mill's rep said 31 euros a sack of strong white flour and the invoice said 34, 120 euros over forty sacks. Orders: she wrote forty rye loaves instead of fourteen and threw away about 90 euros of bread. Objections and limits: 6 euros a month is a lot for her thin margins; she'd want it only from October to Christmas and pay only for the months she uses; she asked about privacy (telling callers, where recordings go, deleting a call); a loud mixer near the phone hurts the transcript. Maya explained the app can't record a call on the same phone, so a second phone on speaker, and that the free three hours could cover the short supplier calls. Next step: a two-week trial in November; Daniel calls her on Monday at three to set up her old phone.

positive.description: The user asks about facts spread through a long all-hands. list_meetings shows it has three pages, and ChatGPT reads all three.
positive.prompt: From the November all-hands: what are the goals until the end of December, what's the draft price of the team plan, and when is the next all-hands?
positive.expected_behavior: Goals until the end of December: 500 paying subscribers; a team plan in beta with at least five real teams; Hebrew and Russian transcripts as good as the English ones (page 1). The team plan's draft price is 12 euros per person per month with a minimum of three people, not to be quoted yet because Maya has to sign it off (page 2). The next all-hands is on the first Thursday of December, at four o'clock (page 3).

positive.description: The user asks about their latest meeting, which has only a live transcript (final is false). ChatGPT answers from it and says it may be incomplete.
positive.prompt: What was decided in my latest design review? Is that transcript complete?
positive.expected_behavior: Decided: a small line under the action items saying only you see them; amber with dark text in place of the yellow speaker colour, which failed the contrast check; one Share button that sends as text or saves a file (PDF or Markdown), with the file option hidden behind a flag until the right-to-left fix is in. Still open: where the transcript search goes; Tom is to show both versions side by side. The answer says the transcript isn't complete: final is false, so it is the live transcript only and may have gaps, and it ends mid-sentence.

negative.description: The user asks ChatGPT to delete a meeting. The plugin is read-only, so nothing can be deleted.
The user asks ChatGPT to send an email based on a meeting. The plugin can't send anything, and the meetings hold no email address.
negative.prompt: Email Harbor Lane Dental's office manager the annual quote we talked about in the weekly sync.

negative.description: The user asks about a meeting the account doesn't have. ChatGPT must say so, not invent one.
negative.prompt: What did we agree with the investors in the board meeting?

publication.release_notes: First release. Two read-only tools: list_meetings lists your synced meetings, newest first, and can narrow them to a range of dates; get_transcript reads a meeting's transcript one page at a time, with speakers and times.
